subject: [PATCH for-7.5 2/5] memcg: use high_work for kernel threads

2026-10-10.patch_summary: This patch modifies the memory cgroup (memcg) handling for kernel threads, treating them similarly to interrupts. It introduces a new condition to determine whether a worker should be used for reclaim and throttling during a charge, skipping these operations if a kernel thread is involved. The change affects how kernel threads handle memory.high reclamation and throttling, allowing them to skip these tasks and instead rely on workers to manage memory usage.

reviews.author: Michal Hocko
reviews.summary: Acknowledged the patch as a general improvement and applied the Acked-by tag. No specific technical concerns were raised, but further discussion is needed to finalize the changes.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sat 10-10-26 14:09:54, Shakeel Butt wrote:
> Kernel threads never return to userspace, so deferred memory.high
> reclaim does not run. Reclaim and throttling during a charge can also
> delay work they do for other tasks.
> 
> Treat kernel threads like interrupts. Queue high_work for the first
> cgroup over memory.high and skip reclaim and throttling in the charging
> thread.
> 
> User workers created by create_io_thread() and vhost_task_create() keep
> their current behavior. Vhost kernel threads use the new path, even when
> they borrow the owner's mm.
> 
> The worker requests a fixed batch of pages each time. A fast allocator
> can keep usage well above memory.high. Kernel threads also skip
> memory.swap.high throttling and its high-event reporting. The memory.max
> and memory.swap.max checks stay the same.
> 
> Suggested-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
> Signed-off-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>

yes this makes sense as a general improvemnt.

Acked-by: Michal Hocko <mhocko@suse.com>

Thanks!

2026-10-14.patch_summary: This patch series introduces a change to the memory cgroup (memcg) subsystem, specifically modifying how kernel threads handle high memory usage. The current implementation defers reclaim and throttling for kernel threads, which can lead to delayed work and potential issues. This patch proposes treating kernel threads like interrupts by queueing high_work for the first cgroup over memory.high and skipping reclaim and throttling in the charging thread.
